notes.text:
Follow-ups from the review of PR #145 (merged), for this card since it branches from that merge and edits the same doctor check:
1. **`src/doctor.js` stale-profile fix text is wrong for a custom-named profile.** It says *drop `allowed_tools` from the profile to take hkb's own list* — true only when `DEFAULT_PROFILES[name]` exists (loadBoard deep-merges over it). For a custom name, dropping the key makes `{allowed_tools}` expand to nothing (`src/dispatch.js:63`) and `--allowedTools` dangles before `--disallowedTools`. Branch the fix text on `DEFAULT_PROFILES[name]`; otherwise say *add Bash(cd *), … to allowed_tools*.
2. **Docs not updated where the behaviour lives:** `docs/harnesses.md` "which layer is actually enforcing" table (the frozen-copy story + the new `worker permissions` doctor line), README's `worker permissions` row, and the wiki (`architecture/overview.md`, `features/web-board.md` now stale for `src/board.js`).
3. Nits worth taking while there: `WORKER_WORKFLOW_FILE` in doctor.js is computed at import (every `hkb` call reads both Actions templates) — compute lazily; the check name differs between ok/warn (`worker permissions` vs `profile <name> permissions`) so `--json` consumers cannot key on it; `test/profiles.test.js` leaves five mkdtemp dirs.
4. Accepted as-is: `VAR=value cmd` prefixes are inexpressible in any allow-list — the PR documents `export VAR=value; cmd` instead.

residual_risk: The dispatch deny is a pattern match on the command line, so an unusual spelling (`hkb  dispatch` with two spaces, an env prefix, a wrapper script) may not match it. hkb's own guard catches those on the profiles where the hook runs (`\bhkb\s+dispatch\b`, DENY_PATTERNS in model.js) but the claude --bg default has only the launch line.

Copilot CLI is still not installed on this host, so `shell(hkb dispatch*)` remains unverified against its parser - which is why it got no deny. If someone verifies that pattern language, Copilot should gain one.

The probes measure Claude Code 2.1.251. Both the space-star deny semantics and the fact that a hook `allow` overrides the native checks are the harness's behaviour, not hkb's, and could change under us; the tests pin what hkb emits, not what the harness does with it.

The `capability` sentence is appended to EVERY deny, including the policy denials (force-push, sudo, kill) where blocking is not really the right answer. Splitting it would need a `kind` on `decidePermission`'s return, and src/model.js was outside this card's scope.

`hkb doctor`'s permission-mode check reads board.json profiles only. A launch frozen somewhere else - a hand-rolled workflow, a wrapper script - is still invisible to it, the same blind spot #138 left on the allow-list check.

The wiki is stale on 5 pages (architecture/overview, adr-004, auto-merge, planning-commands, update-notice). overview.md got a targeted unstamped edit for this card's paragraph only; a `/repolore:refresh` is still owed and was outside this scope.
verification: npm run smoke (launch and template contents changed; 25 content + 3 command + 9 init checks)

node --test test/hook.test.js (6 new: allow -> empty stdout, deny -> the JSON + the block sentence, unknown profile -> empty stdout + stderr, missing KB_PROFILE -> same, no KB_TASK -> nothing at all, file write outside the worktree denied)
node bin/hkb.js doctor on this repo: '/ permission policy', '/ worker permissions  4 allow-lists cover the 16 shell builtins hkb calls safe', permission mode silent

nested `claude -p --permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools "Bash(hkb *)"` (Claude Code 2.1.251, empty temp dir): `hkb dispatch --dry-run` DENIED with --disallowedTools "Bash(hkb dispatch*)", RAN without it, `hkb show 1 --json` RAN with it

results.summary:
Worker policy on the default profile is the launch line, so the launch now closes what a live hook would have closed, and the hook can only subtract from it. Draft PR #159.

**1. `Bash(hkb dispatch*)` at the launch.** A shared `CLAUDE_DENY` in src/board.js:31-42 carries it beside the two force-push patterns; `claude`, `claude-track` and `claude-p` spread the same constant, and the Actions template renders it from a new `{{disallowed_tools}}` variable (src/init.js `actionsFiles`), so the committed .github workflow was regenerated. **Measured**, not assumed — nested `claude -p --permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools "Bash(hkb *)"` against Claude Code 2.1.251, in an empty temp dir, probing `hkb dispatch --dry-run` (writes nothing): DENIED with `--disallowedTools "Bash(hkb dispatch*)"`, RAN without it, and `hkb show 1 --json` still RAN with the flag present. So a multiword space-star deny works, it is what refuses the verb, and `Bash(hkb *)` is not collateral damage. Copilot deliberately gets no deny (its `--deny-tool` pattern language is unverified for that shape) and is told in the prompt.

**2. `preToolHook` is deny-or-silence** (src/hook.js). It writes JSON only for a deny and otherwise exits 0 with no output — a hook `allow` overrides Claude Code's own checks, so an allow would let a `claude-p` worker run what the identical `claude --bg` worker beside it is refused. `KB_TASK` set with `KB_PROFILE` unset or unknown now stands aside with one stderr line instead of running the `{}` policy (which denies `npm test`). Gate unchanged. Every deny carries the way out: `hkb block <n> "needs <what>: <why>" --kind capability`.

**3. Disclose, don't work around** — as prompt text in src/context.js (protocol step 6) and SKILL.md step 2, with the one exception spelled out: a refusal of `hkb complete` means say `hkb finish`, never block.

**4. `hkb doctor` gained `permission mode`** (`checkPermissionMode`/`promptingProfiles`, src/doctor.js): one warning when a launch whose argv[0] is `claude` lacks `--permission-mode dontAsk`, silent otherwise. `claude-action` is excluded — it runs `gh workflow run`, and the triggered run's flags live in the workflow file.

**5. The #145 review follow-ups**, taken here because this card branches from that merge and edits the same check: the stale-profile fix text branches on `DEFAULT_PROFILES[name]` (drop the key only where hkb ships a default to fall back to; a custom name is told to add the patterns, because dropping it expands `{allowed_tools}` to nothing and `--allowedTools` then swallows `--disallowedTools`); `worker permissions` reports under one check name for ok and warn, with the profile/file in the detail, so `--json` consumers can key on it; `WORKER_WORKFLOW_FILE` is rendered lazily rather than at import (every `hkb` call was filling both Actions templates); test/profiles.test.js cleans up its temp dirs via a `scratch(t)` helper.

**6. Stale strings.** init's HOOK_NOTE said "both inert unless KB_TASK is set" — never true of the Stop hook, and the wrong shape for PreToolUse now; harnesses.md's "which layer is actually enforcing" table gained a *what it may answer* row plus the launch-line paragraph and both doctor checks; README's row leads with the launch line and drops "file tools confined to the worktree" as a default-profile feature; docs/manual-mode.md's KB_PROFILE paragraph claimed the `{}` policy still applies.

**For the next worker.** #114 adds `Skill` to `CLAUDE_TOOLS` (src/board.js:24) — unchanged by this card and still a tool name, so it belongs in the `Edit`/`Write` tail, not in `SHELL_TOOLS`. If you add another launch-level refusal, put it in `CLAUDE_DENY` and nothing else needs touching: the three profiles, the Actions template and three tests all read that one constant. The skill version moved 0.5.2 → 0.5.3 (pinned at test/track.test.js:568).
